title: Proposed additions to ontogeny.json for flying fish (Exocoetidae): measured values from a wider literature search
merge_note: Not merged. Same per-field schema as ontogeny.json ({value, unit, kind, species, source{id, cite, doi_or_url, locator}, note}); stage keys match species.flying_fish.stages in ontogeny.json, and only fields with new information are listed. A field may carry `alternatives` (other species or estimates) for the hub to choose between. New stage field pectoral_len_over_SL (unit "fraction of SL") must be added to EXTRA_UNITS in sim-engine/test/ontogeny.mjs. Values under life_history_and_ecology are not state fields. Null fields restate what was searched; they stay null.

kinds.measured: read in the cited primary source
kinds.borrowed: measured, but in another species, stage or condition (named in note)
kinds.derived: computed from sourced inputs by the rule in note
kinds.calibrated: tuned to reproduce a named sourced value
kinds.assumed: no source for the number; reason in note

null_rule: value null = not found (reason says what was searched). Never fill a null by interpolating across it.
value_forms: number | [lo, hi] (a reported range) | boolean | category string
no_bird_data: No Aves data anywhere in this file (holdout).

Ucrit_m_s.reason: not found: no critical swimming speed for any flying fish. Burst and take-off speeds exist (life_history_and_ecology: 3.9-5.2 m/s estimated, ~10 m/s quoted; post-larvae 36 BL/s); a burst speed is not a Ucrit. ff_adult_mass.question: ontogeny.json adult (365 d, SL 0.206 m): 0.1316 kg from the H. affinis length-weight law vs 0.06 kg for the Park & Choi 2010 specimen at 0.203 m SL.
ff_adult_mass.which_species: The 132 g is Hirundichthys affinis (Barbados). The 60 g is Cypselurus hiraii (East Sea of Korea). Different genera.
ff_adult_mass.length_measure: Khokiattiwong et al. 2000 (read in full, p. 51): W(g) = 0.01160 FL^3.01, FL = fork length, n 362. ontogeny.json converts SL to FL with 0.927 (FishBase length-length list, H. affinis: SL = 0.927 FL), so the 132 g is computed correctly. Park & Choi define SL as snout to caudal-fin base (Fig. 2, image read) and measured mass fresh, before stuffing. Both use the stated length type, so a length mix-up does not explain the gap.
evidence: H. affinis at 20.6 cm SL: 132 g (Barbados FL law); 112-125 g (FishShapes museum K 1.28-1.43); ~122 g (Brazil FL laws listed on FishBase, flagged doubtful there).
All 79 FishShapes Exocoetidae specimens have K = 100 W/SL^3 between 0.98 and 2.27 (median 1.43). The Park & Choi models give K = 0.51-0.72.

C. hiraii itself: 101 g mean at 198 mm body length (Shimane 1987, spawning adults), K about 1.3 (if SL) to 1.6 (if FL). FishBase lists C. hiraii maximum length as 20.1 cm SL (a museum catalogue), so the Park & Choi fish were at or above the recorded maximum.

FishBase Bayesian length-weight for C. hiraii (a family-shape prior, not a measurement): a = 0.00646, b = 3.04, TL. It gives 61 g only if 20.3 cm were total length, and about 100-147 g if 20.3 cm is SL.
ff_adult_mass.resolution: Species and length measure are identified. An adult flying fish of ~20.6 cm SL weighs about 112-132 g (H. affinis), and C. hiraii of that size about 100 g. The Park & Choi masses (0.04-0.06 kg) are about half of what their stated SL implies, below all 79 museum exocoetids. The cause is not resolved: a recording or reporting error, or very lean post-spawning fish. Their lift check does not confirm mass independently, because it equates weight with lift at an arbitrary 12 m/s. Recommendation: keep 0.13 kg (H. affinis) as the state mass. Keep Park & Choi for fin areas, spans and aerodynamic coefficients, but do not combine their 0.06 kg with H. affinis SL. For a C. hiraii wing loading use ~0.10 kg (Shimane), not 0.06 kg.

ff_early_growth.question: Larval SL at 3 and 10 d
ff_early_growth.detail: Lab-reared H. affinis grow 0.47 mm/d (4.05 + 0.47 d mm FL), wild juveniles 1.41 mm/d (from 20 mm FL). ontogeny.json assumes a linear ramp from 4 mm at hatch to the von Bertalanffy curve (7.1 mm at 3 d, 14.2 mm at 10 d); the lab line gives 5.5 and 8.8 mm. Other reared exocoetids at 3 d: 3.9-4.2 mm SL (H. coromandelensis), ~7 mm TL (C. hiraii), 7.9 mm TL (P. agoo); at 10 d: 12.0 mm TL (P. agoo). Wild larvae must outgrow lab larvae to fit the wild line (20 mm FL at ~8 d), so the ramp in ontogeny.json is plausible for wild fish and the lab line is a lower bound. Hatch length (3.6-4.5 mm, Hirundichthys) is no longer an assumption.

ff_pelvic_at_hatch.detail: ontogeny.json sets pelvic/SL = pectoral/SL = 0.10 at hatching, from Hunte 1995 ("approximately equal size" in field larvae). Watson 1996 yolk-sac larvae of three genera: pelvic 0.03-0.07, pectoral 0.09-0.13. In Hirundichthys postflexion larvae: pelvic 0.18-0.31, pectoral 0.22-0.52, closer in size, as Hunte says.
